note: A first FY27 guide after 未定 is a real guidance event on a ¥16m/day name (abs_move up), but the same document says any guide shows ordinary profit down on the lost 203m of one-offs, and Q1 faces its strongest comp in three years into rising naphtha, so the two halves nearly cancel and only a small negative lean survives.

A Q1 ordinary loss ~30% worse than a thin single-source consensus is offset by the September 受注速報 landing in the same batch against the easiest comp of the year; no revision is expected at a Q1 and this name has looked through its Q1 losses (+0.39%, -1.14%).

The forecast decision is pre-released (the low-end steer has been public twelve weeks and consensus sits at the ¥5.0bn floor), so holding the range is relief; against that the 全求協 series puts Q2 media revenue at the bottom of the company's own fan with H1 progress far below its 49-60% history, and that miss costs this name only 2-3%.

AEON publishes this name's same-store sales monthly so the H1 shortfall is priced (LESSONS rule 1), the sign of the FY net decision after the 1,745m quake loss is genuinely two-sided, and the only unpriced item is the unsourced 2016 insurance-gain precedent; a 5% realised-vol name with a 1.28% reaction median cannot pay much either way.

This is the one visible-miss case that escapes LESSONS rule 1: Daikokuten publishes no 月次, so a Q1 entering at a 1.2%-margin Q4 run-rate with same-store sales 96.6-98.3 against 103% comps is not computable from a public series, the FY consensus sits only 2.6% below plan, and its last two comparable prints fell 11.5% and 10.5% with 信用倍率 at 8.5x and no short to cover.

The H1 beat is computable from the 64% Q1 progress rate and this register sold the Q1 beat 7.6%; what the release adds is the forecast decision, and with no pre-release 修正 on TDnet against an IFIS number 9% above the company plan a hold is the likelier outcome, partly offset by 3D's 11.63% stake giving a low-probability capital-return tail.

Q1 OP at 65.7% of the H1 plan against 52-54% in the prior two years makes an H1 beat near-certain and an FY upward revision more likely than not on a company that has revised mid-year twice in three years, the PER the stock is quoted on uses the unrevised company number, and Yoshinoya's beat-and-raise five days earlier shows this tape is paying for exactly that.

Aggregating seven individually-disclosed June deliveries (and none in July or August) against last year's 9+2 is work nobody does on a ¥21m/day name with no consensus, pointing to Q1 OP progress of 23-30% against 30-37%; the buy-only margin long at 7.7% of shares and 34 days of turnover was still building into the print and the baseline lean carries no margin component at all, though Fisco's conservatism note and four straight positive Q1 reactions argue the other way.

The SG&A arithmetic is the finding: +9% cost growth and a 6% store count against +5.2% quarterly sales needs gross margin of 21.25-21.3% where the last two quarters fell year on year, while the IFIS Q1 ordinary bar has not moved off -0.6%; the honest counterweight is that two food-heavy peers reporting the same quarter both showed unexpected gross-margin improvement, which is why this is sized well below the arithmetic alone.

The 月次 publish sales and never profit, so the Q2 conversion risk from new-format opening costs and a prize/merchandise mix shift is the unseen part, reinforced by China same-store sales of 76-86% against an overseas plan asking for a +1.4bn swing and by a Q2 FX line that cannot repeat last year's +423m; the same 月次 carry real counter-evidence (accelerating same-store sales, fewer openings than Q1), so each piece is sized small.

The fundamental read is clearly positive — the unseen summer 講習会 quarter needs only ¥1,407m of Q2 ordinary to clear the IFIS H1 bar against ¥1,388m last year, with Kyoshin's +85.5% confirming the season — but the reaction function has veto power here: this register sold both of the last two IFIS beats and has fallen after 7 of 10 prints with 信用倍率 at 16.8x.

A first quarterly print for a newly formed holdco whose larger half loses money at the OP line in every Jun-Aug quarter: consolidated Q1 OP near 6-9% of the 10-month plan sits beside a reported net carrying 77% of the plan from a provisional negative-goodwill gain, which a new retail register may read badly, offset by a plan the predecessors' run-rates say is achievable; the 17% single observation in the baseline is a forecast event, not a quarterly scale.

Large move, no direction: H1 orders +28.1% into a Q3 base of -185m OP points to a 'loss narrowed' headline after a 17% fall into the print, but Q3 is structurally the loss quarter and the printed nine-month progress against a 500m plan implies a Q4 above anything recent on a name with a going-concern note, 324,500 margin-long shares and zero shorts.

The best-documented mechanism on the day: H1 ran at USD ~159 against a 147 plan (and EUR/GBP similarly through), this company has revised its full year at every H1 print since 2022, and its stated 40% payout with EPS at a 39.2% ratio makes a 増配 mechanically implied — the last two such prints paid +7.42% and +11.32%, and consensus is quoted on profit not on the dividend; the Q2 QoQ order drop that cost 7.87% in January is the offset.

A full-year print carrying the new-year guide, so abs_move is high, but last year's identical configuration — a guide 7.4% above consensus into a run-in — fell 5.66%, and this year the stock arrives +7.7% over 20 days and +2.7% intraday; the conservative Q4 and the chance of a quantified 2030-vision upgrade are worth less than that precedent.

USMH cut its FY OP from 100億 to 10億 on exactly the gross-margin pressure Aeon Hokkaido named in its own Q1, and 7512 closed 840/841/841 across that disclosure with no consensus for a cut to land against; the sizes stay small because this name's own mid-year cut cost only -0.45% and 信用倍率 at 0.60 leaves no crowded long to sell.

Q1 OP at 67.9% of the H1 plan against a ~47% norm plus Q2 月次 of +4.6% makes H1 15-22% over plan, and holding the 23,000 FY OP plan would imply H2 OP of 5.4bn against 7.7bn on a weak base, so a raise 10-15% above an IFIS number unmoved for four weeks is live; management held the H1 plan at Q1 despite 68% progress and DCM's margin warning is real, so neither side is sized large.

The two guidance findings contradict each other and I resolve them positive: Eco's publishes no 月次 so its Q2 is unseen, its Q1 ordinary ran at 28.2% of plan against a 24.3% norm while Belc, USMH and Life all fell, the plan already budgets OP -4%, and the stock has been sold 5% with the sector — a held plan on those numbers is 悪材料出尽くし, and this name's last three prints were all bought.

Close to an honest zero: the company told the market in July that Q1 would be a preparation quarter, the one large order since is explicitly 織り込み済み, IFIS equals the plan and no 修正 has been filed, so the only live item is a crowded 7.09x margin long meeting a headline year-on-year decline; abs_move stays high because this name travels and a 1.71% disclosed short is building.

The period and the FY guide were pre-released on 2026-09-14 and the stock took its +13.3% then, so the core's pre-release rule drives both numbers down: the 短信 can only confirm, a second raise four weeks after the first is implausible, and the residual is a 7.5x margin long drifting off the high into a 材料出尽くし print.

Tsuruha, about a third of AEON's H1 operating profit, printed 55.9% of its own full-year plan against 45.7% a year ago and AEON fell 1.3% on the day; AEON's last two H1 prints turned entirely on the H1 OP surprise (-8.66%, +9.40%) and it has not trimmed the plan at an H1 in three years — but the USMH, Ministop, Fuji and AEON FS numbers are consolidated too and the Kumamoto extraordinary loss is unquantified, so the net is only mildly positive.

Q2 sales at 97.4/99.9/96.0 with Kumamoto stores shut puts H1 OP near 12-13bn against a 14.2bn plan while the published ordinary consensus still sits on the 28.4bn plan, and an undisclosed quake loss of the order of the peer's 1,745m is still to come; sizes are small because this name sold even a 14% FY cut by only 1.98%, and the strong September 月次 gives management grounds to hold.

A genuine near-non-result where the two findings offset: the IFIS Q1 bar at 44% of a back-loaded H1 guide looks demanding against last year's 25%, but the ¥150m Radiant cost buried in a Q4 chart slide means the underlying run-rate already exceeds that bar and Radiant consolidates from this quarter.

The 月次 do not pin profit here — last year sales +4.3% came with OP -57% on cost normalisation — so with that step-up now lapped against Q1 existing-store sales of ~107.5% the quarter plausibly prints 900-1,200m against an IFIS Q1 ordinary bar still sitting at last year's depressed 600m; this register buys profit beats hard (+11.87%, +9.31%, +13.18% on actual release dates) and the stock arrives 7.4% lower on a TOPIX transition-measure headline with 信用倍率 at 0.44.

The H1 beat is near-certain (Q1 alone delivered 124m of the 218m plan, leaving 94m needed against 135m last year) and entirely computable from the progress rate kabutan printed in July; on an 8.3% realised-vol name at 208x earnings whose holders own it for the 優待 tickets, last year's identical beat-and-hold moved +0.33%.
